qa.recommendation: Keep the plant as it is and add a note that a data center operator runs on site; do not add a new unit unless a source names a new generator.
qa.note: Digi Power X says it has completed five more modular data center units for North Tonawanda, to be switched on by the end of the second quarter of 2026. It has also reported a load study approval for 60 more megawatts of power at one of its New York sites. That is electric load, meaning power drawn from the grid, not a new generator. The NYISO queue workbook dated August 31, 2026 lists a load request from Digihost Technologies of 50.2 MW in Niagara County, and no gas generation request for the site. The August 2026 EIA planned table has no new generator at the plant. So the 60 MW expansion looks like data center growth, not a distinct new gas unit. I did not find an air permit or a generator filing for a second unit. The state data center moratorium signed July 14, 2026 applies to new large projects of 50 MW or more.

qa.recommendation: Add a note that the gas plant also hosts a crypto mining and possible AI data center business; watch for any new generating unit tied to the 200 MW request.
qa.note: Greenidge Generation operates the gas plant at Dresden and a crypto mining data center on the same site. Its 2025 results release says it won approval for 60 MW of non-curtailable grid power and started a NYISO system impact study for another 200 MW, while it explores AI data center use. The NYISO queue workbook dated August 31, 2026 lists a Greenidge 200 MW data center load request in Yates County. Both are requests for grid power, not for new gas generators. I did not find a new generating unit or an air permit for one.

monitor.note: Alpha Generation, owned by an ArcLight affiliate, proposed on March 16, 2026 to replace six peaking units on barges at the Gowanus and Narrows stations in Brooklyn with three new lower-emission gas units. It answered a Con Edison search for ways to meet a New York City reliability need. The press release does not give megawatts or a start date, and a trade press report says state regulators asked for non-emitting options only. The existing barge stations are not in GEM's New York list that I checked. No air permit has been filed that I found. Check whether the old units are in scope, and recheck once Con Edison or the Public Service Commission picks solutions.
